name: io.github.cyanheads/openfoodfacts-mcp-server
description: Barcode lookup, nutrition search, and product comparison for 3M+ crowd-sourced food products.

tools.name: off_get_product
tools.description: Fetch a packaged food product by barcode (4–40 digits: EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC, and the shorter and longer codes Open Food Facts also holds) from Open Food Facts. Returns the product name and generic name, brand, quantity, ingredients (raw text and parsed list), declared allergens, trace allergens the label warns about, additives, the product-level vegan/vegetarian/palm-oil analysis, computed scores (Nutri-Score a–e and Green-Score, each with the points behind its grade, and NOVA 1–4), the low/moderate/high levels of fat, saturated fat, sugars, and salt Open Food Facts computes, nutrition per serving and per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids, categories, labels, packaging, origins, countries of sale, image URL, data completeness, and when the record was last modified and created. The ingredients text is in the record's main language, named by lang, and can be a contributor's translation rather than what the pack prints; ingredients_text_languages carries the text in every language entered, and image_ingredients_url and image_nutrition_url link the label photos to check it against. Open Food Facts is a crowd-sourced database — a missing field means "not yet entered by contributors," not that the attribute is absent from the actual product. Nutrition is the exception: Open Food Facts returns one preparation state per read, so a read of prepared figures (_prepared keys under nutriments) omits as-sold figures the record can still hold; when that happens, one more product read fetches the as-sold set the record stores into the as-sold fields, and nutriments.stored_as_sold says whether it was read, the record stores none, or it could not be read. Computed scores carry regional formula caveats and are indicators, not absolute rankings; Nutri-Score points rank products of one kind only. Data is under ODbL 1.0 — cite Open Food Facts in downstream use.

barcode.description: Product barcode, digits only: 4–40 digits after any leading zeros. The primary key for Open Food Facts — the barcode of an off_search_products row works as is. Example: "3017620422003" (Nutella FR).

fields.description: Subset of fields to return. Omitting returns all standard fields. Use to reduce payload when only scores or ingredients are needed. A field that cannot be read on its own arrives with what it depends on: nutriments brings serving_size, serving_quantity, and serving_quantity_unit so per-serving figures carry their denominator, serving_quantity and serving_quantity_unit each bring the other plus serving_size, since a quantity reads only with its unit, and nutrient_levels brings nutriments and the same serving fields, since the figures nutriments holds decide its basis. ingredients_text and ingredients_text_languages each bring lang, which names the main language. nutriscore_score brings nutriscore_grade and ecoscore_score brings ecoscore_grade, the grade its points stand behind. requested_fields echoes the full set that was fetched.

items.description: A specific product field to include in the response.

tools.name: off_search_products
tools.description: Search Open Food Facts by full-text query, structured tag filters, or both at once. Returns a summary list with barcodes, product names, brands, quantity (which tells pack sizes of one product apart), Nutri-Score, NOVA group, Green-Score, categories, data completeness, and when each record was last modified and created — enough for triage and selection, not full label data. Use off_get_product on the returned barcodes for complete details. A text query and tag filters combine: every word of the query must match the product name, generic name, categories, labels, or brand, and every filter provided must hold (e.g. query "dark chocolate" with labels_tag "en:organic" and countries_tag "en:france" returns organic chocolate sold in France); numeric nutrient_filters express thresholds per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids, such as sugars below 8 g, and combine the same way, and each row then carries the indexed values the thresholds were checked against; ingredients_tag takes canonical ingredient IDs (e.g. "en:inulin") that must all appear among the ingredients Open Food Facts parsed from the label, and combines the same way; additives_tag is the one exception, filtering only on searches carrying none of query, nutrient_filters, or ingredients_tag. nutrition_grade, nova_group, and ecoscore_grade (Green-Score) each take one grade or an array matching any of them. Tag filter values are canonical tag IDs (e.g. "en:organic", "en:no-gluten") — use off_browse_taxonomy to resolve human terms to tag IDs. A case variant, synonym, or singular of a tag is resolved to its canonical ID where Open Food Facts recognizes it; anything else is matched exactly. exclude_allergens and exclude_traces drop products that declare an allergen or a "may contain" trace, but a product with no allergen or trace data entered passes them, so confirm a candidate with off_get_product before relying on it. At least one search parameter is required. The two paths read different indexes: a search carrying query, nutrient_filters, or ingredients_tag is answered by the text index, a snapshot that lags the live database and whose newest record text_index_as_of dates, while a tag-only search reads the live database and is current, or, where this server keeps a local copy of the Open Food Facts export, can be served from that copy, which source and mirror_as_of then report and whose default order and popularity_key or unique_scans_n sort follow the values stored with each record, so they can differ from a live search, which ranks by its current scan counts — so a recently contributed product can be missing from a text search and present in the same search without query. Data is crowd-sourced; result count reflects contributed products, not all products in the market. Data under ODbL 1.0 — cite Open Food Facts in downstream use.

query.description: Words to find. Every word must match the product name, generic name, categories, labels, or brand — ingredients and quantity are not searched — so put only words the product itself would carry. Punctuation separates words — except an underscore, an apostrophe or period inside a word, and a decimal comma inside a number — so each part of "milk-chocolate" or "salt/pepper" must match, while "l'eau" and "1,5" stay one word. Stop words of English, French, Spanish, German, and Italian ("with", "the", "de", "mit", …) are not required, and neither is a content word that is a stop word in one of them (such as Spanish "soy"), though it still ranks the results. Names are matched in the 31 languages the text index analyzes, so a product named only in French is found by its French name. At most 24 words, counted as runs of letters and digits, so each part of a hyphenated or apostrophe-joined word counts. Example: "dark chocolate 70%". Supplying it routes the search to the text index, a snapshot that lags the live Open Food Facts database and whose newest record text_index_as_of dates; drop it, and nutrient_filters and ingredients_tag, which route there too, to run the same tag filters against the live database or, where this server keeps one, its local copy of the export.

categories_tag.description: Canonical category tag ID. Example: "en:breakfast-cereals", "en:cheeses". Use off_browse_taxonomy with facet="categories" to discover valid values.

brands_tag.description: Brand name as printed, or its slug (lowercased, hyphenated). Example: "nutella", "kellogg-s". A brand name is slugged the way Open Food Facts slugs it — lowercased, common Latin accents dropped, punctuation and spaces hyphenated ("Ben & Jerry's" → "ben-jerry-s", "Nestlé" → "nestle") — and then matched exactly; a search by tag filters alone that reads the live database also resolves brand synonyms. A partial or misspelled brand matches nothing rather than falling back to a near match, so put open-ended brand wording in query instead.

labels_tag.description: Canonical label/certification tag ID, or an array of up to 10 that must all apply. Example: "en:organic", or ["en:organic", "en:fair-trade"] for products carrying both. Use off_browse_taxonomy with facet="labels".

anyOf.description: Up to 10 canonical label tag IDs, all of which must apply.

allergens_tag.description: Canonical allergen tag ID. Example: "en:milk", "en:gluten". Use off_browse_taxonomy with facet="allergens". Selects products that declare this allergen; it cannot select allergen-free products, because a product with no allergen tags may simply have none entered yet. To leave an allergen out, use exclude_allergens.

traces_tag.description: Canonical allergen tag ID the label warns the product may contain as a trace ("may contain nuts"). Example: "en:nuts". Trace tags are allergen tags, so off_browse_taxonomy with facet="allergens" resolves them. Selects products carrying the warning; to leave them out, use exclude_traces.

exclude_allergens.description: Allergen tag IDs a product must not declare, all applied. Example: ["en:nuts", "en:peanuts"]. Each value must be an allergen tag Open Food Facts recognizes — resolve it with off_browse_taxonomy facet="allergens" — and one it does not recognize is rejected rather than sent, because it would exclude nothing. A product with no allergen data entered passes an exclusion, so check a candidate with off_get_product before relying on it.

items.description: One canonical allergen tag ID to exclude, e.g. "en:nuts".

exclude_traces.description: Allergen tag IDs a product's label must not warn it may contain as traces, all applied. Example: ["en:nuts"]. Values are validated like exclude_allergens. A product with no trace data entered passes, so check a candidate with off_get_product before relying on it.

items.description: One canonical allergen tag ID to exclude as a trace, e.g. "en:nuts".

ingredients_analysis_tag.description: Vegan, vegetarian, or palm-oil verdict Open Food Facts computes from the parsed ingredients. Example: "en:vegan", "en:palm-oil-free". "en:maybe-vegan" and "en:may-contain-palm-oil" mean the ingredients could not settle it, and the "-unknown" values mean no verdict could be computed.

ingredients_tag.description: Canonical ingredient tag ID, or an array of up to 10 that must all appear among the ingredients Open Food Facts parsed from the label. Example: "en:inulin", or ["en:inulin", "en:oat"] for products listing both. IDs are singular ("en:oat", not "en:oats"); use off_browse_taxonomy with facet="ingredients" to resolve them, and use ingredients_analysis_tag instead for a vegan, vegetarian, or palm-oil verdict. Each parsed ingredient also carries its taxonomy parents, so "en:vegetable" matches a product listing carrot. Served only by the text index, so supplying one routes the search there even without query — it then reads the lagging text index and is subject to the 10000-result page window, and additives_tag cannot be combined with it.

anyOf.description: Up to 10 canonical ingredient tag IDs, all of which must appear.

additives_tag.description: Canonical additive (E-number) tag ID. Example: "en:e322", "en:e330". Use off_browse_taxonomy with facet="additives". Available only on searches carrying none of query, nutrient_filters, or ingredients_tag — each routes to a backend with no additives field, so combining them is rejected instead of silently returning nothing.

nutrition_grade.description: Filter by Nutri-Score grade, or an array of grades matching any of them. "a" is highest nutritional quality, "e" is lowest. Example: "a", or ["a", "b"] for B or better. A product carries one grade, so an array matches products graded any of its values, unlike labels_tag, whose values must all apply. Products without a score are excluded.

anyOf.description: Nutri-Score grades, any of which a product may carry.

nova_group.description: Filter by NOVA food processing class, or an array of classes matching any of them. "1"=unprocessed/minimally processed, "4"=ultra-processed. Example: "1", or ["1", "2"]. A product is in one class, so an array matches products in any of its classes, unlike labels_tag, whose values must all apply. Products without a NOVA score are excluded.

anyOf.description: NOVA groups, any of which a product may be in.

ecoscore_grade.description: Filter by Green-Score (environmental impact) grade, or an array of grades matching any of them: "a-plus" is the lowest impact, then "a" through "f". "a" does not include "a-plus", so ask for ["a-plus", "a"] for A or better. A product carries one grade, so an array matches products graded any of its values, unlike labels_tag, whose values must all apply. A search by tag filters alone, without ingredients_tag, matches the grade Open Food Facts files for France, while each row shows the world grade, so a row can show a different letter than the one it matched. Products without a Green-Score are excluded.

anyOf.description: Green-Score grades, any of which a product may carry.

countries_tag.description: Canonical country tag ID. Example: "en:france", "en:united-states". Filters to products sold in that country.

nutrient_filters.description: Numeric constraints on nutrient values per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids, combined as AND with each other and with every other filter. Pair two entries on the same nutrient to express a range (e.g. sugars gte 2 and sugars lte 8). Served only by the text backend, so supplying one routes the search there even without query — it then reads the lagging text index and is subject to the 10,000-result page window, and additives_tag cannot be combined with it. The text index compares energy-kcal, fat, saturated-fat, carbohydrates, sugars as whole numbers, so every returned row is checked against these constraints: a row outside them leaves the page and counts in outside_constraints, and a nutrient the index holds no value for does not count against a row. A page can come back short or empty while later pages hold matches, and a range inside one whole number (sugars gt 3.9 and lt 4) can pass few rows of the 10,000 reachable, so add query or tag filters to narrow it. Per-serving and prepared-product values are not searchable.

nutrient.description: Nutrient to constrain, measured per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids. Energy is kilocalories; every other value is grams.

operator.description: Comparison against value: "lt" below, "lte" at or below, "gt" above, "gte" at or above.

value.description: Threshold to compare against: kilocalories for energy, grams for every other nutrient, per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids.

items.description: One numeric constraint on a nutrient value per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids.

sort_by.description: Sort order, applied on every search. Each value orders newest or highest first: "unique_scans_n" surfaces the most-scanned products, "last_modified_t" and "created_t" the most recently updated and newest records, by the times each row carries as last_modified and created, "popularity_key" the most popular. Omitting it leaves text searches relevance-ranked and tag-only searches in the default order. Where this server serves a tag-only search from its local copy of the export (source "off_mirror"), the default order and "popularity_key" and "unique_scans_n" follow the values stored with each record, so they can differ from a live search, which ranks by its current scan counts; "last_modified_t" and "created_t" sort alike.

page.description: Page number (1-based). Use with page_size to paginate results. Pages are counted at the page_size served, which is at most 100, so repeating one larger page_size pages contiguously (page 2 at page_size 200 is results 101–200). A search by tag filters alone that reads the live database is served through page 10 only, so at page_size 100 it reaches the first 1000 matches; where this server keeps a local copy of the export, a tag-only search whose every value it confirms (canonical IDs from off_browse_taxonomy, and a brand it holds products under) is served from that copy through its first 10000 results, so page * page_size (as served) must stay at or below 10000 there. One carrying ecoscore_grade is served from that copy only once a full reload of it has indexed Green-Score. A search carrying query, nutrient_filters, or ingredients_tag serves only the first 10000 results, so page * page_size (as served) must stay at or below 10000. A request past any of these bounds is rejected rather than sent; narrow the filters or change sort_by to bring other products forward. A brand the local copy holds no product under is the exception on a page past 10: one live count answers it empty, with that total, when the live matches end before the page, and rejects it when they reach into it.

page_size.description: Results per page (default 20). One call returns at most 100: a larger value is served at 100, reported in page_size and page_size_capped, and page then counts pages of 100. Keep low for initial exploration; increase for comparison workflows.

tools.name: off_compare_products
tools.description: Side-by-side nutrition and scoring comparison for 2–10 products per call by barcode; a repeated barcode is compared once, so two identical barcodes yield one row, and barcodes past the 10th distinct one are listed in unprocessed rather than fetched. Returns a normalized table of energy (kcal), fat, saturated fat, carbohydrates, total carbohydrates including fiber, sugars, salt, protein, and fiber per 100 g, or per 100 ml for liquids, plus Nutri-Score and Green-Score, each with the points behind its grade, and NOVA group. Open Food Facts returns one preparation state per read, so figures for the prepared product arrive in a prepared object on the row, with the same columns and basis, and never fill an as-sold field; a row whose read returned only prepared figures gets one more product read, of the as-sold set its record stores, once the read of every barcode has settled, with stored_as_sold saying how it went. Designed for "which of these cereals is healthiest?" or "compare these pasta brands" workflows. Missing nutrition data for any product is preserved as absent — comparisons are not imputed. A batch is not all-or-nothing: barcodes that resolve are returned even when others fail, with confirmed-missing barcodes listed in not_found and failed fetches listed separately in failed. Scores carry regional formula caveats; Nutri-Score points break a grade tie only between products of one kind. Data under ODbL 1.0 — cite Open Food Facts in downstream use.

items.description: Product barcode, digits only: 4–40 digits after any leading zeros.

barcodes.description: Barcodes to compare, returned as one row each in input order; a repeated barcode is compared once, so two identical barcodes yield one row. One call compares at most 10 distinct barcodes: up to 100 are accepted, and those past the 10th distinct one are returned in unprocessed without being fetched. Example: ["3017620422003", "7622210100146"].

tools.name: off_browse_taxonomy
tools.description: Resolve a human term to the canonical Open Food Facts tag ID that off_search_products filters on. Covers categories, labels/certifications, allergens, additives, countries, ingredients, NOVA groups, and Nutri-Score grades. Pass a search term to resolve against the Open Food Facts vocabulary, which holds tens of thousands of tags; omitting it returns only a small reference list for each facet except NOVA groups and Nutri-Score grades, which are complete, and ingredients, which has no reference list and returns nothing. Most tag IDs use the "en:" prefix (e.g. "en:organic", "en:no-gluten", "en:crustaceans"); NOVA groups return bare digits "1"-"4" and Nutri-Score grades bare letters "a"-"e". Pass the id through to off_search_products exactly as returned. Category tags are frequently plural ("kombucha" resolves to "en:kombuchas") and ingredient tags singular ("oat" resolves to "en:oat", "oats" to nothing), so use the returned id rather than constructing one.

facet.description: "categories" covers food categories (en:cheeses, en:breakfast-cereals). "labels" covers certifications (en:organic, en:fair-trade). "allergens" covers declared allergens (en:milk, en:gluten). "additives" covers E-numbers (en:e322). "countries" covers country-of-sale tags (en:france). "ingredients" covers the ingredients Open Food Facts parses from ingredient lists (en:inulin, en:oat); it has no reference list, so pass a search term. "nova_groups" and "nutrition_grades" are closed vocabularies returned complete; the other six are resolved against the Open Food Facts taxonomy.

search.description: Term to resolve. Matched case-insensitively as a substring of the tag ID, the display name, or a common synonym of either ("shellfish" resolves to en:crustaceans, "gluten free" to en:no-gluten); the tag the term itself names leads the list even when neither its ID nor its name contains the term as typed ("plant based milk alternatives" → en:plant-based-milk-alternatives). A single word works best ("hummus", not "hummus dip"). Omit only to see a small reference list (none for ingredients) — Open Food Facts cannot list the full vocabulary without a term, so an unfiltered call is not a view of the full facet.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (default 20). One call returns at most 200: a larger value returns the first 200 and, when more matched, says how many did. There is no offset or page input: Open Food Facts offers no cursor for this lookup, so narrow the search term rather than paging. The tag the term itself names (e.g. "lentil" → en:lentils, "US" → en:united-states) is listed first, so it is not the one a small limit cuts.
